child.title: Cleaning rules when there is a small child at home: eco cleaning
child.desc: Eco cleaning for a healthy stay of your baby at home, followed by iCleaning's specially trained home eco-care specialists.
child.seo: Eco cleaning when there is a small child at home

body.x: Why do we need eco cleaning? The arrival of a child in the family is a special joy and responsibility. “Keeping the house clean” — for many young parents these words take on a new meaning. After all, the smaller the baby, the more vulnerable the little body. We often hear that a child has a stuffy nose or complaints that the child is often ill. All sorts of things are blamed: viruses, colds, teething. But a visit to the doctor is not enough to find the cause of the trouble. It is important to carry out an ecological examination of the apartment. The cause may be invisible to the eye but noticeable to a small body — house dust, fungus, mold.
First of all, pay attention to the ecology of the children's room, because this is where the child spends most of the time.

x: Furniture and decoration should be made of the most natural materials possible. Artificial substitutes can be toxic and cause unexpected allergies.
Every nursery must have large, bright windows that can be opened for regular airing.
The fewer soft toys, fluffy (currently popular) blankets, bedspreads and rompers that collect dust and become carriers of germs, the healthier your baby will be.

body.x: But how can we do without all this? Carpets give us comfort, and in the cold season warmth too. The baby is learning to crawl and taking first steps, so it must be safe and comfortable. And toys — loved ones so like to give them. How can you deprive relatives of the joy of presenting a huge teddy bear for the baby's first birthday? And how many positive emotions it gives a child to ride a plush horse or cuddle a toy panda cub of real size!

Soft toys, sofas, carpets and even walls accumulate dust and the tiniest particles of our everyday life (clothes, toys, newspapers). When we vacuum, these microparticles are dispersed and settle on the surfaces of our interior and on our belongings.

Consequently, a constant companion in our home and the cause of many diseases is dust. We tirelessly try to fight it. But while for some it is only a nuisance and an inconvenience, for a small child dust is often a source of illness. Why does this happen? Bacteria and viruses cannot fly on their own, and dust lifts them into the air. It is a kind of “flying boat” for disease-causing agents. Besides, dust itself can cause allergies.
What should you do?

Prepare the apartment for the baby's arrival and clean it properly. For this there is an eco cleaning algorithm for a comfortable and healthy stay of the baby in the apartment, followed by iCleaning's professionally trained home eco-care specialists.
What is eco cleaning?

First of all, you need to remove dust from surfaces very delicately and competently and achieve cleanliness without chemicals. Non-toxic professional organic-based products can help. A must is the use of microfiber, excluding rags and wipes that shed dust, as well as anything with any impregnation (antibacterial or chemical).
An excellent alternative to household chemicals is universal cleaning products such as vinegar, lemon and baking soda.
For example, you can disinfect children's toys in soapy water with a small amount of white distilled vinegar.
You can get rid of mold and soap scum in the bathroom or shower by wiping the surface with the same undiluted vinegar and then rinsing with water.
And if after renovation you need to wash floors without streaks — one glass of vinegar per liter of water guarantees cleanliness and shine.
An ordinary lemon will help you wash dirty kitchen countertops. Cut it in half and sprinkle a spoonful of baking soda on it. And while this mixture is fizzing, start wiping.

These remedies probably take a little more time. But they are completely ecological and do not cause allergies. iCleaning's professionally trained home eco-care specialists can save you time and effort by using only eco products and eco chemistry. They will thoroughly and quickly remove the sources of contamination in your home and create a good environment for the healthy development of your baby.

fridge.title: Smell in the fridge? Top 7 ways to get rid of it
fridge.desc: 7 ways to get rid of the smell in the fridge: want to quickly and permanently remove an unpleasant smell from your fridge? Follow iCleaning's advice!
fridge.seo: Smell in the fridge? 7 ways to get rid of it!

body.x: Every kitchen has a fridge. Whether it is an apartment or an office, it tirelessly keeps food fresh. But one day, when we open the door, we want to close it again very quickly. The reason is an unpleasant smell in the fridge.
So what should you do to get rid of the smell in the fridge?
First of all, you need to understand the cause of this phenomenon, because your fridge most often smells for the following reasons:

x: Improper food storage. Cover pots, jars and containers with a lid or cling film. Try not to forget about foods that give off a far-from-pleasant aroma when they spoil.

The fridge was bought recently. Its walls still have the tiniest plastic particles and the smell of machine oil and metal. In this case it is enough to wash the appliance thoroughly inside and out, wiping all the shelves and fittings. You can use a baking soda solution or a weak ammonia solution (five drops per liter of water). Then wait a little while the smell airs out.

body.x: Now that we understand the cause, let's try to eliminate it with the simplest and most effective methods.

We will consider only organic remedies, which are used by iCleaning's home eco-care specialists, because the fridge is a place of contact with food. It is not advisable to use chemicals here so as not to harm your health.
1. Vinegar.
In first place is the “king” of cleaning — vinegar.

Take out all the food and wipe the walls, shelves and fittings thoroughly. To do this, dilute 9% vinegar with water in a ratio of one to one and wash the whole fridge with the solution. Pay special attention to the drain and the seal. This simple and inexpensive method will rid you not only of the unpleasant smell in the fridge but also kill up to 90% of all bacteria, germs and mold. If you are worried about the specific smell of vinegar — it is not a problem. Even if you don't wipe the treated surface dry, the vinegar will evaporate without a trace in a couple of hours.
2. Ammonia.
Second place goes to ammonia.

Dilute a teaspoon of ammonia in a liter of water, mix and wipe your fridge well with the solution. Thanks to the alcohol, no streaks are left on the surface, it dissolves grease well and washes away the germs that cause the unpleasant smell in the fridge.
3. Baking soda.

Effective against fungi and excellent at absorbing odors, baking soda rightfully takes the next place. First, wash your fridge with a water solution — two tablespoons of soda per liter of water. Then pour some soda into a small container and put it in the fridge, changing it once every three months.
4. Lemon juice.

Lemon juice will help fill the appliance with freshness. Squeeze a little from a lemon and moisten a cloth. Wipe thoroughly, then cut a lemon (or an orange) into wedges and put them on a saucer, leaving them for 2–3 days. Lemon is especially effective at removing the smell of fish.
If you have a small child or your schedule is booked minute by minute and there is no time to wash the fridge thoroughly, iCleaning's home eco-care specialists will definitely help you with this.
Now that your fridge has already been washed, open its door for a couple of hours to air it out well. And if a little smell remains in the fridge, the following will help eliminate it:
5. Activated charcoal.

Crush 30–40 tablets, put them on a saucer and leave in the fridge until the smell is gone (5 days at most). It is worth noting that some housewives always keep charcoal on the shelf as a preventive measure. And not in vain, since charcoal is part of many odor absorbers sold in stores.
6. Rice, salt and sugar.
They can also be put on a saucer and placed in the fridge. To prevent unpleasant smells, change them every few days.
7. Raw potatoes.
A natural adsorbent is peeled raw potato and an onion cut into several pieces. Lay these foods in the corners of the fridge on paper napkins or saucers and change them every 2–3 days.
And remember, a stale smell in the fridge is not only unpleasant: all the food gets saturated with it, which is especially dangerous for your health. Keep things clean and live healthy!

bath.title: Secrets of eco-friendly bathroom cleaning
bath.desc: Safe cleaning in the bathroom? Not sure where to start? iCleaning specialists will tell you the rules of eco-friendly bathroom cleaning.

body.x: How do you clean the bathroom so that no streaks are left on the shower cabin and the tiles shine like new? How do you clean without harming your health?

If you have small children, allergy sufferers, pregnant or breastfeeding women at home, or you simply care about your health, eco-friendly bathroom cleaning is exactly what you need. There are several ways to do it.
The cheapest and simplest way is to tidy up with what you always have in the house (lemon, salt, vinegar). Steam and organic household chemicals are also safe and effective.
Rules of eco-friendly bathroom cleaning

When you start cleaning, it is important to remember the “golden” rule of professional cleaning: wash and clean from top to bottom and from the inside out (first wash the inner surfaces, then the outer ones, which are less dirty).

That is why you should clean the walls first. Traces of limescale are often visible on them. To remove them easily and quickly, use a vinegar solution. You can read how to prepare it in the article “Cleaning rules when there is a small child at home: eco cleaning”. And to fix the result, just wipe the surface with a microfiber cloth.

If the grout between the tiles has become dirty, an ordinary toothbrush with baking soda (or vinegar, toothpaste, fine kitchen salt) will help you. Never use soap to clean grout — it promotes the spread of mold spores. Re-grouting takes time and effort. To save them and relax in a professionally cleaned bath afterwards, contact iCleaning's home eco-care specialists. They will put everything in order quickly and thoroughly.

When your walls shine like new, it is time to wash the bathtub. Today the most common ones are cast-iron, steel and acrylic tubs. But how should they be cared for properly? Modern acrylic tubs are the most delicate. It is best to wash their surface with a soft sponge and liquid soap. If there is a small child in the house, baby soap is better than household soap. And warm table vinegar or lemon juice will easily remove rust-water stains from the surface.
And so as not to destroy the enamel layer of a cast-iron or steel tub, do not remove stubborn dirt from the surface with sand, sharp objects or alkali.

If you own a shower cabin, which is so prone to deposits from hard water, vinegar will help. It is a universal and inexpensive product. Thanks to its acetic acid content it is a powerful disinfectant. It “kills” harmful bacteria such as salmonella, E. coli and the agents of dysentery. So take ¼ cup of vinegar, 2 cups of water and half a teaspoon of an organic cleaning product. Shake in a spray bottle and clean with pleasure. When finished, wipe with a microfiber cloth.

Next in line for cleanliness is the sink. Yellow stains often form on it from water and soap. Removing them is very easy. Mix a small amount of warm vinegar with one or two pinches of table salt. Apply this to a washcloth and rub. A little effort and the sink is like new. The toilet can be washed the same way.

An integral part of the bathroom is the plumbing fixtures. To restore their mirror-like cleanliness, use toothpaste. Apply it to a sponge and rub. You can also make taps shine with a lemon wedge, and then wipe them dry with a microfiber cloth.

If mold has appeared in your bathroom, get rid of it as soon as possible. Its spores are toxic and cause allergies, and they affect children and the elderly most, whose bodies are the most susceptible. So just apply vinegar to the affected area, let it soak in and wash it off with an ordinary sponge. If you decide to fight mold, be sure to eliminate sources of moisture.
When your bathtub is sparkling clean, it is time to finish the cleaning by washing the door and the floor. Read here how to do it properly.

You can also clean the bathroom effortlessly with a steam cleaner. Dirt, rust and limescale on plumbing and walls are no match for it. linen.title: 8 tips for choosing children's bedding
linen.desc: Choosing children's bedding often seems a difficult task. iCleaning's tips will help you make the right choice.

body.x: Healthy sleep is the key to your child's physical and emotional health. To a large extent it depends on choosing the right bedding. It would seem such a small thing, but it is bed linen that affects your baby's mood throughout the day — and therefore yours too.
When choosing bedding for your child, follow these rules
1. Quality of fabric

First of all, pay attention to the fabric the bedding is made of. To avoid provoking allergies from an early age, choose natural materials — satin, chintz, calico. The manufacturer usually states the fabric composition on the label.

When choosing bedding for newborns, remember that at first it will be washed especially often, so it must be durable. That is why satin linen suits best. It is stronger than calico and very soft, which is important for the baby's delicate skin.
2. Durability of the material

Poor-quality fabric quickly “loses its look”, becomes thinner and begins to show through. Pay attention to the density of the material, which the manufacturer usually indicates on the label in grams per square meter. The higher it is, the better, of course.
3. Color

According to psychologists, the color of your child's bedding largely determines the child's psychological state and the quality of sleep. So when choosing linen for a baby, look at items in calm and natural shades. Never use the acid colors that are popular today — they have an exciting effect on the nervous system of a small child. Ideal choices are soft blue, pink, green and beige with unobtrusive pictures of teddy bears, elephants and the like. In short, those that will attract the baby's attention and help them get to know the world.
If you are choosing bedding for an older child, take the following into account:

x: Blue bedding suits an active child. This color helps relieve the emotional tension accumulated during the day.

Bedding in soft shades reminiscent of tasty treats — cinnamon, chocolate and caramel — should be chosen for those who eat poorly or refuse breakfast altogether. Psychologists say that after using bedding of this color for a month, the result will not keep you waiting and the child's appetite will return.
Be careful with purple linen. This color depresses the nervous system and can provoke a bad mood.
Avoid dark, gloomy colors in your choice, giving preference to colorful and cheerful shades that will help your child develop their imagination.

body.x: 4. Dyeing method

Choose items dyed with natural dyes. They do not fade, do not cause allergies and will not stain the baby's skin during sleep. You can recognize chemical dye by sniffing the item — it has an unpleasant smell.
5. The seam the fabric is sewn with
Quality linen is made with a flat-felled seam. Also pay attention to the edges. They must be hemmed.
6. Size of the bedding
A comfortable bed is the key to your child's healthy sleep. That is why choose linen by size, so that extra ends do not bunch up or hang down to the floor collecting unnecessary dust.
7. Safety in bed

When choosing linen for the youngest, pay attention to the duvet cover fastening. They come in different kinds — zippers, Velcro, buttons. Some do not fasten at all. Those suit older children. For babies, it is safe to buy items with a side zipper, so that they do not get tangled or swallow buttons.
8. Bedding for the age

Respect your child's preferences. Choose bedding according to their age and interests. If a boy loves a cartoon about cars, give him joy by buying bedding with his favorite characters. In that case, going to bed, the child will feel comfortable and protected, which will contribute to sound sleep.

Be attentive when choosing bedding for your child. And do not forget that, according to research by the British Daily Mail, the bed is the dirtiest place in your home. For this very reason 34% of Britons face allergy symptoms. So, to keep your child healthy, change the bedding at least once a week and periodically deep-clean the mattress the baby sleeps on. plants.title: Useful houseplants, or how to survive in a metropolis
plants.desc: Houseplants — which of them are useful specifically for a city apartment? It turns out a flower can protect you from the flu, relieve stress and improve your health.

body.x: When buying houseplants for our home, we usually pay attention to their beauty and how they match the interior. But we do not always think about the benefit they will bring to our home. It turns out, though, that a flower can protect you from the flu, relieve stress and improve your health.

The champion of room purification is chlorophytum. It is easy to care for and useful. It cleans polluted air superbly and absorbs formaldehyde, whose sources in an apartment are often tobacco smoke, gas stoves, scented candles and carpeting. If someone in the house is ill, chlorophytum will clear the room of harmful bacteria quite quickly. It is no accident that pests never attack it. And to strengthen the plant's cleaning properties, put a few activated charcoal tablets into the flower pot.

In winter you cannot do without a ficus. By releasing phytoncides, it will protect you from colds, humidify dry air and saturate it with oxygen. That is why it is best placed in the living room and the kitchen. The glossy leaves of a ficus hold a lot of dust, so they need to be wiped often. And experienced flower growers recommend not watering the plant in winter, only misting the leaves.

The ideal flower for a bedroom is aloe. At night it purifies the air, releasing oxygen and absorbing carbon dioxide. And during the day it reduces static electricity in the apartment. Many people keep aloe at home for its medicinal properties. If you have caught a cold or have a headache, its juice will certainly help. And a washed leaf of the plant is useful when applied to a bleeding or infected wound.

Geranium is an excellent antidepressant. It will help you relax during stress and overcome insomnia. Just put it in the bedroom. Requiring no special care, it will give you sound and peaceful sleep. And because geranium releases biologically active substances that kill staphylococci and streptococci, it disinfects the space, repels flies and absorbs dampness and fumes, so it will be especially useful in your kitchen.

A true helper for the lady of the house is the begonia, familiar to many. This small bush with bright irregularly shaped flowers attracts dust excellently and humidifies the air. In addition, it destroys up to 80% of fungi and disease-causing microbes, reducing the effect of radiation from computers and household appliances.
A real oxygen factory is sansevieria, or “mother-in-law's tongue”. The plant will rid your apartment of dryness and stuffiness and clear the air of unnecessary formaldehyde.

And if you have recently done a renovation, iCleaning's professionally trained home eco-care specialists will definitely help you put things in order. You can read about the secrets of eco cleaning here.

Even in a cleaned apartment, the smell from new building materials and furniture is simply unavoidable. People often try to remove it with artificial air fresheners, which have an adverse effect on the body, especially a child's. But there is a way out. A unique plant and natural filter is the peace lily (spathiphyllum). It is very undemanding and easy to care for. It is enough to put it in the apartment after renovation, and within a few days the fumes of acetone, ammonia and benzene and the smells from plaster and new furniture will be significantly reduced. The plant is so effective that in a one-room apartment a single pot is enough.
To absorb the harmful fumes of linoleum and exhaust gases, the parlor palm (chamaedorea) will help you. Just a couple of plants can significantly improve the air quality in the apartment.

To avoid getting sick, get a lemon tree or an eucalyptus. They release substances that reduce the number of disease-causing components in the air by almost half. And by relaxing the smooth muscles of the bronchi, they relieve spasms. That is why these plants are useful for asthmatics, and it is easy to breathe near them.

Houseplants will bring you benefit only if they are clean and healthy. Dust is very harmful to flowers. It clogs the pores and hinders moisture evaporation and gas exchange, which disrupts the plants' absorption of carbon dioxide and the production of useful substances.

To prevent this, flowers need proper care. First of all, to remove dust, wipe the plants with a damp sponge. Flowers with downy and folded leaves, and cacti, should be dusted with a brush. Then send the plant to the shower. Pots can be placed right in the bathtub and the leaves washed with a stream of water. And so that the soil in the pot is not washed out, cover it with polyethylene film.

It is desirable to give your flowers a “bath day” at least once a month.
